title: Probing Myosin Ensemble Mechanics in Actin Filament Bundles Using Optical Tweezers
protocol: Dissolve 100 g of KOH in 300 mL of 100% ethanol in a 1,000 mL beaker.
Stir with a stir bar until the majority of the KOH has dissolved.
Place coverslips individually in coverslip cleaning racks.
Prepare and label three 1,000 mL beakers: one with 300 mL of ethanol and two beakers with 300 mL of reverse osmosis (RO) water.
Place each of the four beakers in a bath sonicator to degas for 5 min.
Submerge a rack of coverslips in the beaker of KOH and ethanol and sonicate for 5 min.
Transfer the rack of coverslips from the KOH/ethanol beaker to the ethanol-only beaker.
Dip rack up and down in the beaker until there is no beading.
Transfer the rack of coverslips from the ethanol beaker to a beaker of water.
Dip the rack up and down in the beaker until there is no beading observed.
Submerge the rack of coverslips in a new beaker of water.
Sonicate the rack of coverslips for 5 minutes.
Spray the rack of coverslips with water to ensure it runs off smoothly.
Repeat spraying with ethanol.
Place the racks in an oven at 90 °C for 20 minutes to dry.
Store the etched coverslips in closed containers at room temperature.
In a 50 mL conical tube, add 3.94 g of Tris-HCl and 0.147 g of CaCl2.
Add RO water to make a total volume of 50 mL and mix well.
Label the tube as Solution T.
Store Solution T at 4 °C.
In a 50 mL conical tube, mix 40 mL of RO water with 1.5 mL of Solution T.
Adjust the pH to 8.0 by adding small amounts of concentrated KOH.
Add water to make a final volume of 50 mL and verify the pH.
Label the tube as TC Buffer.
Store TC Buffer at 4 °C.
In a 100 mL buffer bottle, add 85 mL of RO water, 10 mL of Solution T, 3.73 g of KCl, and 0.041 g of MgCl2.
Adjust the pH to 7.5 by adding small volumes of concentrated KOH.
Add water to make a final volume of 100 mL and verify the pH.
Mix 485 μL of TC buffer, 10 μL of 10 mM ATP, and 5 μL of 50 mM DTT in a microcentrifuge tube to prepare GAB.
Label the prepared GAB and store it at 4°C.
Mix 455 μL of FC buffer, 25 μL of 100 mM ATP, and 20 μL of 50 mM DTT in a microcentrifuge tube to prepare APB.
Label the prepared APB and store it at 4°C.
Reconstitute rabbit skeletal muscle actin by adding 100 μL of deionized water to a vial of lyophilized actin.
Mix well by gently pipetting up and down.
Aliquot into 5 μl samples, snap-freeze, and store the 10 mg/ml actin aliquots at -80°C.
Reconstitute biotinylated rabbit skeletal muscle actin by adding 20 μL of RO water to a vial of lyophilized actin.
Aliquot into 5 μl samples, snap-freeze, and store the 1 mg/ml biotinylated actin aliquots at -80°C.
Thaw one vial of 10 mg/ml actin and keep it on ice.
Prepare fresh GAB buffer by mixing with deionized water if necessary.
Add 100 μL of freshly prepared or stored GAB to the thawed actin aliquot, mix gently.
Incubate the solution on ice for 1 h.
Thaw one vial of 10 mg/mL actin and 1 vial of 1 mg/mL biotinylated actin on ice.
Combine the two vials in a 10:1 actin:biotinylated actin ratio.
Add 100 μL of GAB to the actin mixture and mix well by gently pipetting up and down.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 1 hour.
Prepare fresh APB during the incubation period.
After incubation, add 11 μl of APB to the actin solution and mix well by gently pipetting up and down.
Place the mixed solution on ice for 20 minutes.
Add 5 μL of rhodamine-labeled phalloidin to the freshly polymerized actin filament solution.
Leave the mixture on ice in the dark for 1 hour.
Store the rhodamine actin vial wrapped in aluminum foil in the dark at 4°C.
Reconstitute lyophilized skeletal myosin II by briefly spinning down (~5 s) in a standard minicentrifuge to collect it at the bottom of the tube.
Add 100 μL of 1 mM DTT prepared in RO water to reconstitute myosin to 10 mg/mL.
Dilute the stock myosin solution 10x by adding 10 μL of 10 mg/mL myosin to 90 μL of 1 mM DTT in RO water.
Make small-volume (1-5 μL) aliquots, snap-freeze, and store at -80 °C.
Dilute 20 μL of 1 μm streptavidin beads into 80 μL of RO water.
Wash the diluted streptavidin beads four times by spinning down at 9,600 × g and reconstituting in 100 μL of RO water.
Sonicate the washed beads for 2 min at 40% amplitude.
Store the washed beads on a rotator at 4 °C.
Prepare a poly-l-lysine solution (PLL) by adding 30 mL of 100% ethanol to a 50 mL tube and then adding 200 μL of 0.1% w/v poly-l-lysine in water, mixing well.
Add an etched coverslip to the PLL solution and allow it to soak for 15 min.
Remove the coverslip with tweezers, ensuring only the edge is touched as it is pulled up from the tube.
Dry the coverslip with a filtered airline until there is no ethanol left and no residue on the coverslip.
Apply two pieces of double-sided sticky tape to the middle of a microscope slide, 3-4 mm apart from each other.
Cut off excess tape hanging off the edge of the slide.
Place a PLL-coated coverslip on top of the tape perpendicular to the long axis of the microscope slide.
Use a small tube to compress the coverslip onto the tape and microscope slide thoroughly until the tape is transparent.
Ensure there are no bubbles in the tape as this can cause leakage from the flow channel.
Dilute each type of actin filament (rhodamine- and biotinylated 488-labeled) 600x by mixing 0.5 μL of labeled actin with 300 μL of APB in separate tubes.
Add an additional 5 μL of correspondingly labeled phalloidin to each tube.
Incubate the mixture on ice in the dark for 15 min.
To the biotinylated actin solution, add an oxygen scavenging system consisting of 1 μL of beta-D-glucose at 500 mg/mL, 1 μL of glucose oxidase at 25 mg/mL, and 1 μL of catalase at 500 units/mL.
Add 1 μL of 100 mM ATP to the biotinylated actin solution.
Add 1 μL of 100x diluted, cleaned streptavidin beads to the biotinylated actin solution.
Gently stir the suspension with a pipette tip.
Put the suspension on a rotator at 4 °C.
Add 15 μL of the diluted rhodamine actin to the PLL flow cell.
Wick the excess solution through the flow cell without allowing it to become dry.
Incubate for 10 min in a humidity chamber.
Prepare a 1 mg/mL casein solution in APB.
Add 15 μL of 1 mg/mL casein to prevent non-specific binding.
Incubate for 5 min in a humidity chamber.
Mix the desired concentration of myosin with the biotinylated actin and bead suspension from step 5.2.
Immediately add 15 μL of the mixture to the flow cell.
Incubate for 20 min.
Seal the open ends of the flow cell with nail polish to prevent evaporation during imaging and optical trapping experiments.
Turn on the control box.
Turn on the laser.
Start the optical trap computer software by clicking on the JPK Nanotracker icon on the desktop.
Wake up the remote controller by clicking on the Logitech button at the center.
Turn on the fluorescence module by toggling the on/off switch.
Turn the filter cube turret for brightfield imaging.
Turn the laser using the Laser Power button to 50 mW and let it stabilize for 30 min.
Click on the Illumination button within the software.
Click on the Camera button within the software.
Click on the Objective button within the software.
Click on the Stage Movement button within the software.
Turn the microscope illumination on by clicking the On/Off button.
Set the illumination power to maximum by dragging the bar all the way to the right.
Open the sample area and remove the sample holder from the microscope stage.
Add a flow cell and secure it with metal sample holders.
Place the slide with the coverslip in the bottom position.
Add 30 μL of RO water to the center of the bottom objective without touching the lens with the pipette tip.
Reinsert the sample stage.
Raise the lower objective using on-screen control arrows or L2 on the remote controller until the bead of water touches the coverslip.
Lower the top objective until about half the distance to the flow cell is reached using on-screen arrows or R2 on the remote controller.
Add 170 μL of RO water to the top of the flow cell directly under the top objective.
Lower the top objective until it breaks the surface tension and forms a meniscus.
Move the microscope stage using the arrow pad on the remote controller until the edge of the tape adjacent to the flow channel is reached.
Close the sample door.
Bring the edge of the tape in focus using the bottom objective by clicking the upper arrow using the on-screen controls.
Bring the top objective down into focus by clicking the bottom arrow using the on-screen controls.
Partially close the iris at the top of the optical trap.
Bring the edges of the polygon shape of the iris into focus.
Reopen the iris.
Click on the Padlock icon to couple the objectives.
Find a floating bead and trap it by clicking on the Trap Shutter button.
Drag the Trap cursor to move the location of the trapping laser.
Calibrate the trapped bead to correlate voltage measurements to force and displacement.
Click on the Calibration button within the software.
Adjust the calibration routine based on power spectra analysis.
Fit the corner frequency for X, Y, and Z directions within the software.
Type in the diameter of the bead (1,000 nm).
Enter the temperature of the stage found in the bottom left of the software window.
Click on Trap 1.
Click on X Signal.
Run to perform the corner frequency fit for X direction.
Optimize the function fit by clicking and dragging within the window.
Use It for sensitivity and stiffness values for X direction.
Accept Values for X direction calibration.
Repeat for Y and Z signals.
Close the window after completing calibrations.
Find an actomyosin bundle by searching for beads bound to AFs on the surface of the coverslip.
Verify the presence of a bundle by observing the AFs around it using fluorescence imaging.
Verify that a bundle is present by looking for both fluorescent AFs colocalized.
Turn on the white light source.
Use the appropriate filter cube to image each actin filament.
Turn the turret to use 488 nm and 532 nm excitation filter cubes for Alexa Fluor 488 and rhodamine excitation, respectively.
Trap the bead attached to the top filament of the bundle by clicking on the Trap Shutter button.
Use the on-screen controls to record the data by clicking on the Oscilloscope button.
To visualize measurements without recording the data, click on Start.
To save all data, click on Autosave.
To record measurements, click on Start Record.
Choose which data are to be visualized in real-time from the drop down menu X signal or Y signal.
Remember that x-direction is left to right and y-direction is up and down on the screen.
